rows.item: Bathtub overflow — waste arrangement when overflow is provided
rows.code: 2025 California Plumbing Code (CCR Title 24, Part 5), Section 404.2 Overflows
rows.value: Where a fixture is provided with an overflow, the waste shall be so arranged that standing water in the fixture cannot rise in the overflow when the stopper is closed and cannot remain in the overflow when the fixture is empty. Overflow pipe connects to the house/inlet side of the fixture trap.
rows.source_label: 2025 California Plumbing Code, IAPMO official e-publication (Chapter 4)
rows.notes: Confirmed via IAPMO official e-pubs of the 2025 California Plumbing Code; section text also quoted in IAPMO Uniform Codes Spotlight (forms.iapmo.org/email_marketing/codespotlight/2019/Jan31.htm).

rows.item: Concealed waste and overflow materials (typical bathtub installation)
rows.code: 2025 California Plumbing Code, Section 404.2 (per IAPMO Code Spotlight)
rows.value: When waste and overflow fittings are concealed, as in most bathtub installations, they must be constructed from materials approved for drainage pipe.
rows.source_label: IAPMO Uniform Codes Spotlight quoting CPC Section 404.2
rows.notes: IAPMO is the publisher of the California Plumbing Code; the spotlight reproduces Section 404.2 language. Material approval should be confirmed with the installing contractor and SF DBI inspector.

rows.code: California State License Board (CSLB), Class C-36 plumbing contractor
rows.value: A C-36 license is required for plumbing work valued at $500 or more (labor + materials). License status, bond, and disciplinary history are publicly verifiable at cslb.ca.gov.
rows.notes: CSLB official site confirms C-36 classification covers installation/repair/maintenance of plumbing systems; $500 threshold per California Business & Professions Code as summarized by CSLB guidance.

rows.item: San Francisco plumbing permit — when required
rows.code: San Francisco Building Code, Section 104.0 Permits (exemptions)
rows.value: Exempt work includes 'replacement, repair or maintenance of faucets, angle stops, hose bibbs or roof drain not requiring cutting into or removal of piping.' Work requiring cutting into or removal of piping (e.g., opening the wall to reach concealed overflow plumbing) falls outside that exemption and likely requires a plumbing permit. Confirm with SF DBI.
rows.source_label: San Francisco Building Code §104.0 (official SF code library, American Legal Publishing)
rows.notes: AmLegal is the official publisher of the San Francisco Code. The specific exemption boundary for this job must be confirmed with SF DBI before work.

rows.item: San Francisco DBI — plumbing permit and contractor requirements
rows.code: SF Department of Building Inspection (DBI), Online Permits & Scheduling
rows.value: Plumbing contractors must hold a valid California contractor license (C4 or C36 for plumbing permits), a valid San Francisco business license, workers' compensation certificate, and DBI contractor database registration to obtain plumbing permits via DBI Online Services. Central Permit Bureau: 49 South Van Ness Avenue, 2nd Floor.
rows.notes: SF DBI official page. DBI also notes 'replacement in kind requires DBI permit equivalent to new work' (SFDBI Division of Plumbing Inspection document). Confirm permit need for this specific job with DBI.
